descriptions.text: Hunting Trophy. It's the hand of a hunter. Gross. You own 34 of these items. You ever go to one of those arcade pizza joints as a child? You're usually there because it's some other kid's birthday, or worse, because your parent hates raising you so much they'd do anything just to keep you distracted for ten minutes in exchange for a pitcher of watered-down beer. The whole place is chaos. …

recap.text: Carl pulls the mantis claw of Xindy from his inventory while Donut opens a box of her own, and a gray hand pops out. Its description says the hand is a ticket for the prize counter at the Butcher's Masquerade, where the cheapest award costs one hand. A trap Carl left kills a hunter, and he holds up JayGee's hand and tells JayGee's friends to go fuck themselves. Chaco the Bard says Carl has 66 hands to spend.

beats.headline: Thirty-four boxes of hands
beats.text: Thirty-four Hunter Killer boxes line up in a row that floats all the way to the wall, and each holds gold and a hand. The first is the mangled claw of Xindy, the mantis Carl blew out of the sky with his rockets. The second is the hand of Chin'dua, the drunk draconian. The third is an orc's. None of them wear rings. All that, Donut says, and it's a bunch of horrible hands. At least it's not tongues: Lucia Mar collects tongues.
beats.gist: Thirty-four Hunter Killer boxes hold gold and a hand each, and Donut calls them horrible hands.

beats.headline: A prize ticket
beats.text: Carl pulls the mantis claw from his inventory and examines it while Donut opens her own box, and a gray hand pops out. The description wanders through arcade pizza joints and a prize counter where forty dollars of tickets buy five cents of bubble gum, then gets to the point: the hand is the ticket. The prize counter where it may be exchanged opens at the Butcher's Masquerade, near the end of this floor. The cheapest award costs a single hand. Transfer or sell one, and it reverts to some dude's appendage.
beats.gist: A Hunting Trophy, a hunter's hand, works as a prize ticket, and the cheapest award costs one hand.

beats.headline: JayGee's hand, held high
beats.text: A trap Carl left kills a hunter, and the gold Hunter Killer box holds 35,000 gold and the fat, mottled gray hand of a hunter named JayGee. Carl holds the trophy up to the ceiling and waves it: if JayGee's family or friends are watching, they can go fuck themselves. You shouldn't do that, Mordecai says. People out there have long memories. Good, Carl says. He doesn't want them to ever forget.
beats.gist: JayGee's trap-killed hunter yields 35,000 gold and a hand; Carl waves it, defying warnings of long memories.

beats.headline: Fifty-two trophies now
beats.text: Most of Carl's new boxes are low-tier adventurer boxes, but fourteen are Hunter Killer boxes, including the one from Future Hunter the orc. He now has fifty-two hunting trophies.
beats.gist: Fifty-two hunting trophies sit in Carl's inventory after new boxes, fourteen of them Hunter Killer boxes.

beats.headline: Sixty-six hands to spend
beats.text: Chaco the Bard stands behind the prize counter in the ballroom. You currently have 66 hunter hands, he tells Carl. Wow. Every purchase arrives as a prize box, and upgrades are installed at once. The items turn on a vertical carousel as miniature holograms. A single hand buys a 25-pack of good healing or mana potions; two buy one upgrade from a row, plus ten percent to a lowest stat, plus five percent to a highest, or plus two to a random combat skill or spell; three and five buy potions and scrolls by the dozen; thirty buy a future floor boon; fifty, full sets of armor. One prize costs a hundred hands.
beats.gist: Chaco the Bard's prize counter sells items for hunter hands, and Carl has 66 to spend.
